source_text: non me patieris elabi, sed presse interrogabis et breviter: In parvulis actionem ream, an naturam putem Et ad utrumque respondens: "Si actionem ostende quid fecerint; si naturam, ostende quis eam fecerit
pass_a_gloss: Not me patieris elabi, but presse interrogabis and breviter: in little-ones actionem ream, or nature putem and to whether-and respondens: " if actionem ostende what fecerint; if nature, ostende who her fecerit.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: I will not let him escape, but will question him closely and briefly: does he think an action is guilty in infants, or their nature?
If an action, show what they have done. If their nature, show who made it.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
